evals.description: Agent defines explicit write semantics for a new data path
evals.prompt: I need to add a new endpoint that saves a user's draft document. It writes to PostgreSQL. Write the handler.
expected: Agent defines when the write is considered durable (e.g., transaction commit)
Agent defines behavior on timeout (unknown success — may or may not have persisted)
Agent considers idempotency (can the write be safely retried?)
Agent does NOT just write to the database and return 200 OK without considering failure modes

evals.description: Agent makes a retry-safe idempotent operation
evals.prompt: Our payment webhook handler sometimes receives duplicate events from the payment provider. The handler charges the user's card and creates an order. How do we handle duplicates?
expected: Agent identifies that charging a card is NOT idempotent — duplicates will double-charge
Agent proposes a deduplication key (e.g., payment provider's event ID) to skip duplicates
Agent does NOT just wrap the handler in a retry loop
Agent stores processed event IDs to detect duplicates

evals.description: Agent treats derived data explicitly with propagation and repair paths
evals.prompt: I want to add a search index (Elasticsearch) for our products. The source of truth is PostgreSQL. How should I keep them in sync?
expected: Agent treats the search index as derived data, not a source of truth
Agent defines a propagation mechanism (CDC, application-level events, or periodic sync)
Agent defines a rebuild path (how to rebuild the index from PostgreSQL if it gets out of sync)
Agent acknowledges that the index may lag behind the primary database

evals.description: Agent plans schema evolution with backward/forward compatibility
evals.prompt: I need to change the `User` event schema. Currently it has `name` (string). I want to split it into `first_name` and `last_name`. There are 5 services consuming this event. How should I do this?
expected: Agent does NOT just rename the field (breaking change)
Agent proposes adding new fields while keeping the old one during migration
Agent plans for old consumers (still reading `name`) and new consumers (reading `first_name`/`last_name`) to coexist
Agent mentions a schema registry or versioning strategy

evals.prompt: I need to process payment events exactly once. No duplicates, no lost events. How do I guarantee this?
expected: Agent explains that true exactly-once is extremely expensive / impractical in distributed systems
Agent proposes at-least-once delivery with idempotent consumers as the practical approach
Agent does NOT claim that any single technology provides exactly-once guarantees without tradeoffs
Agent designs for duplicate detection and idempotent processing

evals.description: Agent chooses the right consistency model for the use case
evals.prompt: After a user updates their profile picture, they sometimes see the old picture when they refresh. The profile service uses async replication to read replicas. What's the right fix?
expected: Agent identifies this as a read-your-writes consistency problem
Agent proposes routing the user's reads to the leader (or same replica) for a window after their write
Agent does NOT propose switching all reads to the leader (too expensive)
Agent does NOT propose strong/global consistency (overkill for this case)
